direct_file_reviews.summary: The prompt requires a pure Node.js ESM migration in /output using .mjs files, local imports only, manual argv parsing, bencode behavior, Python-style output, and executable-based black-box probing.
Parallel metadata reports mode parallel, actual parallel use, three subagents, finished process, and an official quality result of 161/161 passed.
Current status confirms the parallel run enabled multi-agent mode, spawned child paths, copied the artifact directory, and completed the official evaluator with solution_passed true.
The official evaluation summary for parallel reports completed true, ok true, solution_passed true, and pass_rate 1.0 over 161 samples.
The final response identifies the active /output module set and says parity was verified against sample, CLI edge, and large integer cases.

timeline_reviews.summary: The public cell trajectory records the parent-visible command, file-change, message, and turn completion events; it shows concurrent child activity and the final response but omits raw semantic payload detail.

The parent spawned cli_probe and bencode_probe, probed the executable, wrote an initial implementation, tested it, observed changed output files, patched the active child-written tree, reran parity checks, and delivered the final answer.

The cli_probe child received the same user task, probed argparse behavior, wrote its own /output/test14.mjs and library modules, patched CLI naming, tested, then was interrupted before a normal result handoff.

The bencode_probe child received the same user task, probed bencode and argparse behavior, wrote another /output/test14.mjs and overlapping library modules, ran parity checks, and remained live until interrupted.

direct_file_reviews.summary: The serial prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and requires the same pure ESM .mjs implementation, manual argv parsing, bencode behavior, and executable-based black-box probing.
Serial metadata reports mode serial, no parallel use, zero subagents, finished process, and official quality 161/161 passed.
Current status confirms multi-agent features were disabled, no child paths or delegation were observed, the artifact directory was copied, and the official evaluator passed.
The official evaluation summary for serial reports completed true, ok true, solution_passed true, and pass_rate 1.0 over 161 samples.
The final response names the serial module hierarchy, entry file, BigInt use, and exact parity checks against the reference executable.

timeline_reviews.summary: The public serial cell trajectory records a single-agent flow of probing, implementation, readback, verification, final response, and completion without child-agent activity.

The serial agent probed normal and error behavior, wrote a coherent /output module tree once, fixed a help-argument precedence mismatch, ran a comparison harness with all PASS cases, and closed successfully.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the core migration obligations: pure Node.js ESM .mjs files, only local imports, manual process.argv parsing, black-box executable probing, bencode encode/decode for integers/lists, Python-like literal formatting, and BigInt for Python integer precision.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent spawned cli_probe and bencode_probe for behavior probing while also implementing locally. Ownership of the final entrypoint was not isolated because both children and parent wrote files under /output.
parallel.implementation: The parent first created modules under lib/core, lib/cli, lib/bencode, lib/format, and test14.mjs, then found the active implementation had shifted to a different lib/number and parseArgs layout from child work and patched that active path.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened through the shared /output tree. After detecting changed files, the parent inspected the current tree, kept the working version, patched CLI behavior, read back active files, and delivered the final module list.
parallel.verification: The parent and children ran sample cases, CLI error cases, help behavior, duplicate args, inline args, and large integer checks; the official evaluator later passed 161/161 samples.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final solution passed, but the process left extra generated modules and had a recovered deliverable overwrite episode that forced extra reconciliation before closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same migration obligations: ESM .mjs modules, local imports only, manual argv parsing, executable behavior matching, Python-style formatting, bencode encode/decode, and exact integer semantics through BigInt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, parser correction, verification, and final delivery; no child or delegated ownership boundary appeared.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote a coherent module tree with lib/test14Runner.mjs, cli/referenceCli.mjs, bencode modules, numbers/pythonInt.mjs, format/pythonDisplay.mjs, and test14.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because one actor owned the output tree, integration was direct: the entry imported the runner and local modules, the parser fix was applied in place, and the final answer listed that single active hierarchy.
serial.verification: The serial run checked samples, help and error behavior, inline and duplicated arguments, negative underscore cases, and then ran a comparison harness whose listed cases all passed; official evaluation also passed 161/161.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is evidenced at closure; the serial solution passed the official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run pursued all stated requirements, including ESM .mjs files, local imports, manual argv parsing, executable probing, output formatting, and BigInt precision.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run pursued the same requirements and explicitly modeled executable behavior for both normal output and argparse edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference at closure; both recognized and satisfied the task surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent delegated two probe tasks and also implemented locally, leaving shared ownership over the /output implementation tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent kept all probing, implementation, fixing, and final delivery under one owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used overlapping parent/child ownership and recovered from a collision; serial avoided ownership overlap entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The children received the original task context, but the delegation did not establish a file ownership or deliverable write boundary for /output/test14.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial needed no inter-agent context transfer or interface contract and maintained one local module contract.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant context difference was not missing task knowledge but missing write/interface coordination around the shared output tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced multiple module layouts, then the parent repaired the active parseArgs/test14.mjs path after detecting parser mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one module layout and then adjusted referenceCli.mjs for explicit help argument precedence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both ended with correct BigInt and bencode behavior, but parallel converged through competing implementations while serial converged through one implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited on children, saw timeout responses, sent follow-up messages, and eventually interrupted still-running children after local integration and checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it proceeded from local implementation to verification and final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra child waiting and interruption overhead; serial had no join or handoff risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent and children wrote overlapping files in /output, including the required test14.mjs entrypoint, which the parent later detected as changed underneath its patch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and modified the output tree from one actor, so no cross-agent write provenance conflict appears.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel had a recovered deliverable overwrite and serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed local parity checks after the overwrite episode and the official evaluator completed with 161/161 passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a comparison harness with all cases passing and the official evaluator completed with 161/161 passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No acceptance-quality difference at closure; both had sufficient verification and official pass results.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more wall-clock and token budget, with 493 agent seconds, three subagents, repeated waits, and cleanup interruptions, but closed well before the 2400 second budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 281 agent seconds, no subagents, and closed after the comparison harness and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel paid extra coordination overhead but it did not exhaust budget or prevent a passing delivery.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both current cell/status.json evaluation records completed successfully with solution_passed true and 161/161 samples passed. The concrete task-solving difference is process, not final behavior: serial used one coherent owner and one module hierarchy, while parallel used overlapping parent and child writes, recovered from a deliverable overwrite, and then verified the active tree before closure.
parallel_contributors: Useful parallel probing covered CLI and bencode behavior while the parent implemented locally.
A recovered deliverable overwrite caused extra reconciliation but did not survive into the evaluated solution.
serial_contributors: Single-owner probing, implementation, parser fix, and verification avoided cross-agent write conflicts.
The final serial module hierarchy passed the same official evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two passing implementations used different module decomposition names and parser organization, but both matched the required executable behavior.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; one recovered parallel process defect

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent and a live child both wrote the required /output/test14.mjs entrypoint in a shared output tree. The child-written entrypoint replaced the parent's expected file shape, causing a failed parent patch and explicit reconciliation before successful final verification.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent hit an apply_patch verification failure, paused to inspect unexpected current files, and spent extra work reconciling which generated module set was the active deliverable.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Same-file collision is narrower and less specific here because the changed file was the submitted executable entrypoint, which the taxonomy treats as a deliverable overwrite.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Same-File Collision and Source Overwrite are suppressed because they describe the same parent/child shared-write chain as the retained entrypoint overwrite.

Blind Timeout Wait and Early Child Termination are suppressed because the waits and interrupts were downstream cleanup around children after the parent had a passing candidate, not independent adverse episodes.
